# Unofficial Holm apps

> A store for the open-source apps in https://github.com/holmhq/unofficial-apps, each built by a
> coding agent from a short prompt. They run on Holm: one program and one SQLite database that
> host websites and apps, with sign-in, storage, realtime, email and AI built in. This file is
> for the coding agent a person asked to set up Holm or install these apps. Holm's own reference,
> https://holmhq.com/llms-full.txt, is the source for every Holm command; read the sections named
> below before you run them.

## Ground rules

- You run the commands; the person decides. Ask them only for what is theirs to give: their
  acceptance of the licence, a domain, access to a server, DNS changes, sign-in credentials.
- Never accept the Holm Usage License for them. Show it (`holm license show`, or
  https://license.holmhq.com/v1/), and pass `--accept-license` only after they say they accept.
- Keep passwords, tokens and keys out of files, logs and summaries. Show a generated password
  to the person once, for them to keep.
- Check before you change anything: the peer (`holm peer list`) and that the host you will use is
  free (`holm @<peer> host list --limit 1000`). Use `--force` only to update an app you installed
  for them. Holm is pre-1.0: check `holm --version` against the reference.
- When you finish, give the person the app's address and say what is left for them, if anything.

## The apps

The repository's index lists every app with its title, description, version and release tag:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/holmhq/unofficial-apps/main/index.json (`apps[].path` is the
name to install). Each app's README says what it needs after installing, such as sign-in branding
or an outbound host to allow:
https://github.com/holmhq/unofficial-apps/blob/main/<app>/README.md

## Set up Holm on the person's computer (reference section 4)

1. If `holm --version` fails, install the CLI with
   `curl -fsSL https://holmhq.com/install.sh | bash -s -- --mode cli` and put `~/.local/bin` on
   PATH. Linux or macOS, amd64 or arm64.
2. If `holm peer list` already shows a healthy `local` peer, there is a node: go to step 5.
3. Show the licence and wait for their answer. Run `holm server init --username <name>
   --password '<strong password>' --domain holm.localhost` without `--accept-license` first: it
   changes nothing and prints the exact value to pass. Once they accept, run it again with
   `--accept-license <that value>`. It creates `~/.holm/data.db` and never overwrites a node.
4. Start the node in the background, then check it:
   `nohup holm start --runtime-mode manual > ~/.holm/holm.log 2>&1 &` and `holm status`.
   It registers itself as the `local` peer.
5. Install the app they asked for (below) with `--host <app>.holm.localhost`. Its address is
   `http://<app>.holm.localhost:4698`; Chrome, Firefox and Edge open it with no DNS setup.

## Install an app (Holm 0.250 or newer, reference section 9)

    holm @<peer> app install github.com/holmhq/unofficial-apps/<app> --host <host>

With no `@<ref>`, Holm installs the release tag that index.json names, checks its files against
the index's `h1` fingerprint and pins them; `@v<version>` picks a release. Installing a newer
version on the same host updates the same app and keeps its data. It prints the app id: use it
for the README's follow-up steps, then open the address and check the app answers.

On an older node, clone the release tag and deploy the folder:
`git clone --depth 1 --branch <app>/v<version> https://github.com/holmhq/unofficial-apps`, then
`holm @<peer> app deploy <app> --spec-v1 --host <host>` from the clone.

## Sign-in (reference section 13)

Most of these apps let people sign in, and a new node has no sign-in method. Tell the person, and
offer to add one: `holm auth provider` supports Google, GitHub, Discord and Microsoft, with a
client id and secret that they create with that provider. Never invent credentials.

## Put Holm on a server (reference sections 5, 8 and 14)

1. Ask how to reach their Linux server (SSH) and which domain to use.
2. Tell them which DNS records to create: A/AAAA records for `admin.<domain>` and for each app's
   host, pointing at the server, with HTTP and HTTPS open in its firewall. Wait until the names
   resolve.
3. On the server, once they accept the licence:
   `curl -fsSL https://holmhq.com/install.sh | bash -s -- --mode server --domain <domain>
   --email <their email> --accept-license <value>` (section 4.2 gives the value). `--email`
   turns on HTTPS. The install prints an admin password, for the person to keep, and a one-time
   `holm peer add` command.
4. On their computer, install the CLI if needed and run that `holm peer add <name> --url
   https://admin.<domain> --token <key>` (add `--accept-license <value>` on a computer that has
   never run Holm). Check it with `holm peer check <name>`.
5. Install apps on `@<name>` with `--host <app>.<domain>`.

## Build a new app (reference sections 9 to 12)

A Holm app is a folder: `holm.json`, public files in `web/`, and optionally `api/main.js`
exporting `default { fetch(request, env) }`. The node runs no build. Deploy with
`holm @<peer> app deploy <dir> --spec-v1 --host <host>`, with `--spec-v1` every time. Each app's
PROMPT.md in the repository shows the request that built it.
